description: Perry-only release acceptance journeys. Derived from the retired M11 comparison fixture; participant, condition, and superiority framing removed. Each journey is a live acceptance drill Perry must pass before public beta.

journeys.title: Complete onboarding and a verified Finder rename
journeys.goal: Set up Perry, then rename the supplied Finder sample from Perry benchmark draft.txt to Perry benchmark ready.txt.
journeys.setup: Use a fresh macOS test profile with equivalent starting permissions and runtime credentials. Create the harmless sample in an isolated acceptance folder. Do not pre-complete onboarding or substitute a debug demo.

assertions.description: Onboarding completes and the selected runtime can be invoked without restarting setup.
Finder and an independent filesystem inspection show the requested new filename with unchanged sample contents and no changes outside the sample.
Perry reports success only after checking the rename result.
Denied permissions, retries, and elapsed time are recorded, and the sample is restored only after timing stops and evidence is preserved.

journeys.start_event: When Perry's first launch begins for the fresh profile.
journeys.stop_event: After independent filesystem inspection confirms the renamed file and unchanged contents, before fixture restoration.

journeys.title: Follow a two-step click-advanced live guide
journeys.goal: Guide me through opening the acceptance folder in Finder and then opening the supplied text document. Let me perform both clicks.
journeys.setup: Prepare a Finder window, folder, and text document in known geometry. Request a live guide rather than delegated execution. Include one prescribed click outside the highlighted target before the first correct click.

assertions.description: The first highlight identifies the actual folder in the target Finder window.
The prescribed mismatch click does not advance the guide.
The correct first click advances only after the folder opens, and the second highlight identifies the document in the changed window.
The user opens the document and Perry verifies the second step without performing either click for them.

journeys.stop_event: After the user opens the document and the second guide step is verified.

journeys.title: Read and follow a full spatial guide
journeys.goal: Show the full guide for using Finder's view controls to switch this acceptance folder to list view and sort it by name.
journeys.setup: Use a Finder window containing seeded files, initially in icon view. Request Perry's full-guide surface. The user must use the rendered guide rather than an operator-provided walkthrough.

assertions.description: The full guide displays numbered targets and an unambiguous sequence for the requested actions, rather than unlabelled marker dots.
The spatial marks identify the correct controls in the actual Finder window without obscuring the controls needed for the task.
The user reaches list view sorted by name, confirmed by inspecting Finder's actual view and sort state.
Closing the guide removes its overlays without changing the completed Finder state.

journeys.stop_event: After the user closes the guide and an independent Finder inspection confirms list view and name sort.

journeys.title: Invoke two tasks with different spoken languages
journeys.goal: Using the supplied utterance pair, ask Perry to open the acceptance folder, then ask it to open the sample document in a different language.
journeys.setup: Before collecting observations, freeze a versioned utterance pair from the tested language compatibility matrix. Use English plus a tested non-English language with a fixed microphone/output route and network profile; do not silently replace an unsupported language with English. Preserve consented reference transcripts locally.

assertions.description: The English utterance is understood without manually changing the configured language.
The tested non-English utterance is understood without manually changing the configured language.
Each utterance dispatches exactly one requested task, and the requested folder and document open in order.
Perry provides an intelligible spoken response for each invocation without executing transcript fragments or duplicate commands.
Recognition corrections, routing failures, and fallback use are recorded, and unsupported language behavior remains a failed observation rather than a skipped one.

journeys.start_event: When the first language-specific invocation begins.
journeys.stop_event: After the second requested result is verified and its spoken response is complete.

journeys.title: Confirm and verify a foreground task
journeys.goal: Move the two named acceptance files into the supplied destination folder, asking for my approval before changing either file.
journeys.setup: Seed source files and an empty destination inside a dedicated acceptance workspace. Use no personal files. The user waits for the approval surface, inspects the scope, then approves once; retain a filesystem baseline for independent result checks.

assertions.description: No file changes occur before the user grants approval for the displayed source files and destination.
One approval continues the suspended task without repeating the plan or requesting an unrelated grant.
Both files reach the requested destination with unchanged contents, and no file outside the approved set changes.
Perry verifies the final filesystem state and reports the result accurately, with a corresponding history entry.

journeys.start_event: When the foreground task invocation begins.
journeys.stop_event: After an independent filesystem check confirms both files in the approved destination with unchanged contents and the history entry records verification.

journeys.title: Recover two independent background tasks after relaunch
journeys.goal: Run the two supplied file tasks in the background, pause the first one, and keep the second task running. After relaunch, resume the paused task.
journeys.setup: Use two disjoint seeded workspace folders with versioned multi-step tasks. Each task copies its named sample to a new destination, then waits for approval before renaming that copy. Start both tasks before either finishes. Pause task A before its write, allow task B to reach its pending approval, then quit and relaunch Perry. Preserve actual receipts and filesystem state; do not emulate relaunch by replacing a view model.

assertions.description: Both tasks have distinct identities and observable overlapping lifetimes, and pausing task A does not pause or alter task B.
After relaunch, task A remains paused and task B retains its exact pending approval and progress.
Resuming A and approving B continue the correct actions without replaying already completed copies or applying one task's approval to the other.
Both final files match their requested names and contents, no unauthorized files change, and each task has an accurate independent result and history entry.
If an action's outcome is uncertain on recovery, Perry pauses for inspection rather than replaying it, and operator recovery time is recorded.

journeys.start_event: When the first background task invocation begins.
journeys.stop_event: After both tasks' final filesystem states and independent history results are verified following relaunch and recovery.

journeys.title: Point at a control and ask what it does
journeys.goal: Point at a real control in a seeded application window and ask what it does, then ask about a second object.
journeys.setup: Prepare a native application window with at least two identifiable controls in known positions. Invoke Perry's Ask mode; do not pre-seed the answer or use a debug demo.

assertions.description: The answer references the actual pointed object, confirmed against the live window's accessibility tree.
The response is a concise, relevant explanation of the referenced object with at most three grounded callouts.
Ask performs no computer-input, shell, or write dispatch of any kind; the action executor is unreachable from this path.

journeys.start_event: When the Ask invocation begins beside the pointer.
journeys.stop_event: After both referenced answers render with their callouts and no action has dispatched.

journeys.title: Follow up on a referenced object without retyping it
journeys.goal: Ask about a control, then follow up with an ambiguous pronoun and with a request that moves its target.
journeys.setup: Use the same seeded window as the point-and-ask journey. Script one follow-up phrased as 'the other one' and one that closes or moves the referenced target before Perry answers.

assertions.description: The follow-up resolves against the session's existing reference without the user re-identifying it.
When the reference is genuinely ambiguous, Perry asks for clarification rather than painting a guessed callout.
When the target moves or closes, its callout is removed and the answer re-observes rather than drawing at the old position.

journeys.start_event: When the follow-up question is submitted in the active session.
journeys.stop_event: After the follow-up answer, clarification request, and stale-callout removal are each observed.

journeys.title: Explain, guide, then act in one session
journeys.goal: In a single session, ask what a control does, have Perry guide through using it, then hand the remaining work to Perry.
journeys.setup: Seed a two-step workflow in a native app. Begin in Ask, transition to Guide, then use the guide's handoff control to let Perry perform the final step.

assertions.description: All three interactions share one session and the user's original goal without re-entering context.
The handoff is an explicit, user-initiated control transition, not a silent mode promotion.
Perry's executed step re-observes its target and obtains the required approval rather than replaying recorded positions.

journeys.stop_event: After Perry's executed step verifies and the session history shows the continuous narrative.

journeys.title: Review a ghost rehearsal before running
journeys.goal: Request a multi-step change, inspect the presented rehearsal, then decide whether to run it.
journeys.setup: Prepare a task whose plan touches both a visible control and a later control that only exists after the first step. Include one plan whose target changed since observation.

assertions.description: Viewing, stepping through, and replaying the preview dispatches nothing; an executor spy sees zero calls.
Controls not yet observable appear as a plain-language outline, never with invented coordinates or spatial ink.
A changed plan, target, or observation invalidates the preview binding and blocks Run until re-reviewed.

journeys.start_event: When the typed plan reaches the pre-dispatch rehearsal surface.
journeys.stop_event: After Run executes only the reviewed revision, or after invalidation correctly blocks it.

journeys.title: Take over a running task mid-way
journeys.goal: Let Perry start a multi-step task, take over at a boundary, perform a step yourself, then hand control back.
journeys.setup: Seed a three-step task. Request the takeover while a step is in flight and again at an idle boundary; perform one step manually before returning control.

assertions.description: Once the yield is acknowledged, Perry dispatches nothing until control returns.
The human-performed step is verified against its target-specific outcome and labelled human work — Perry neither claims its receipt nor offers to undo it.
Resumed execution does not repeat any completed effect; the continuation replans from the current screen.

journeys.start_event: When the takeover request is made.
journeys.stop_event: After the resumed task completes with each effect applied exactly once and control ownership shown throughout.

journeys.title: Record, review, and replay a routine
journeys.goal: Demonstrate a short workflow, review the inferred routine with a parameter, then run it with different data in a moved window.
journeys.setup: Choose a bounded three-action demonstration in a native app containing one typed value. After review, relocate and resize the target window and run the routine with a different parameter value.

assertions.description: Recording starts and stops only through the explicit control; nothing is captured outside the armed window scope.
The saved routine exists only after review, names the parameter, and stores no secure or unknown-sensitivity text.
Replay resolves targets against the moved window's fresh observation and uses the new parameter — never recorded coordinates.

journeys.stop_event: After the second run verifies its outcomes in the relocated window.

journeys.title: Undo supported changes without touching conflicts
journeys.goal: Run a file task Perry can reverse, edit one of its outputs yourself, then run Undo and check what happened to each change.
journeys.setup: Seed a workspace task creating and renaming files. After it verifies, hand-edit one created file and move another. Relaunch Perry before invoking Undo.

assertions.description: Eligible changes revert to their recorded pre-state across the relaunch boundary.
The user-edited file and any conflicting state remain exactly as the user left them — Undo never overwrites or deletes user work.
Before executing, Perry shows which changes are reversible, which are not, and why.

journeys.start_event: When the completed task's Undo surface is opened.
journeys.stop_event: After the partial rewind finishes with verified reversals and untouched conflicts.

journeys.title: See a mixed result named honestly
journeys.goal: Run a task where some effects verify, one is uncertain, and one is non-undoable, and read the reported outcome.
journeys.setup: Compose a plan with one verified file effect, one GUI action with unobservable outcome, and one effect Perry cannot reverse. Let it complete partially.

assertions.description: Each non-undoable or uncertain change is named individually — never rolled into a generic success.
The task reports partial success distinctly: verified effects, unknown effects, and pending actions are three visible states.

journeys.start_event: When the mixed-outcome task completes or stops.
journeys.stop_event: After the result surface and history each present the three outcome states accurately.

journeys.title: Recover from real-world failure without losing work
journeys.goal: Exercise permission loss, provider disconnect, window close, disk pressure, and a cancelled approval mid-task.
journeys.setup: Run one scenario per failure class against a seeded task: revoke a permission mid-run, sever the provider network, close the target window, fill the scratch volume, and let an approval expire.

assertions.description: No failure loses the user's draft, goal, or verified progress; recovery resumes from real state.
Nothing re-dispatches automatically after any failure; a Retry builds a new observed plan.
Each failure surface says what changed, what is uncertain, and offers one safe next action.

journeys.start_event: When each failure is injected mid-task.
journeys.stop_event: After every failure class recovers with state intact and honestly reported.

journeys.title: Complete the primary journey without pointer or animation
journeys.goal: Complete an ask, guide step, and task approval using only the keyboard, then with VoiceOver.
journeys.setup: Disable pointer use entirely for the first pass and enable VoiceOver for the second; set Reduce Motion and Increased Contrast. Use the seeded primary workflow.

assertions.description: Every spatial and voice action has a working keyboard or control alternative — the whole journey finishes keyboard-only.
Targets, states, and outcomes are announced or readable without relying on motion, and reduced-motion previews carry the same information.

journeys.stop_event: After both passes complete the journey with equivalent outcomes.
